title: Proof of interface knot markov z
html:
Proof. Proof of interface knot markov z

Proof (Markov axiom + Hecke skein)

For a positive interface generator \sigma_g, the Markov axiom (thm:jones-markov-trace) gives

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha \cdot \sigma_g) \;=\; z \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha)
  \qquad \forall\, \alpha \in H_{n}(q).

For a negative interface generator \sigma_g^{-1}, the Hecke skein relation \sigma_g^{-1} = \sigma_g - h \cdot \mathbf{1} combined with linearity of \mathrm{tr}_M gives

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha \cdot \sigma_g^{-1})
  \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha \cdot \sigma_g) - h \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha)
  \;=\; (z - h) \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha).

Iterating over the p_+(K) + p_-(K) interface generators of \bowtie_K — each one is "topmost" relative to the constituent sub-braid below it — and applying the appropriate factor per sign yields the boxed identity (\star).

Averaged (bar-invariant) p-n interface

The same single Markov input fixes a third interface factor. The canonical p-n boundary (closed_form_tau_M.canonical_interface_kinds, prop:averaging-resonance-rule) carries no preferred chirality, so it is the bar-invariant (q \leftrightarrow q^{-1} symmetric) crossing

  \sigma_{\mathrm{bar}} \;:=\; \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(\sigma_g + \sigma_g^{-1}\bigr)
  \;=\; \sigma_g - \tfrac{h}{2}\cdot\mathbf{1},

the last equality again from the Hecke skein \sigma_g^{-1} = \sigma_g - h. Linearity of \mathrm{tr}_M then gives

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha\cdot\sigma_{\mathrm{bar}})
  \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha\cdot\sigma_g) - \tfrac{h}{2}\,\mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha)
  \;=\; \Bigl(z - \tfrac{h}{2}\Bigr)\cdot\mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha).

Thus all three per-interface factors — z (positive), z-h (negative), z-\tfrac{h}{2} (bar-invariant p-n) — follow by trace-linearity from the single Markov axiom \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha\sigma_g) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha) plus the skein \sigma_g^{-1}=\sigma_g-h; none is an independent input or a fit. The division-free form \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha(\sigma_g+\sigma_g^{-1})) = (2z-h)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha) is formalised over a generic commutative ring as interface_knot_markov_z_bar_symmetric (the \tfrac12 normalisation is deferred to the archimedean realisation, per the base-ring convention).

The three factors are one bar-orbit

Writing \overline{\phantom{x}} for the involution q \mapsto q^{-1}, the positive and negative factors are bar-conjugates of each other:

  \overline{z} \;=\; \frac{q^{-3}}{q^{-2}+1} \;=\; \frac{1}{q\,(q^{2}+1)}
  \;=\; z - h .

So f_{pp} = z and f_{nn} = \overline{z}, and the p-n factor is exactly their mean,

  z - \tfrac{h}{2} \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(z + \overline{z}\bigr),

which is the bar-symmetriser of z — manifestly bar-even. The name "bar-invariant p-n interface" is therefore literal rather than descriptive: the p-n factor is not merely a bar-invariant choice, it is the bar-symmetrisation of the p-p factor.

This also fixes where a flavour weighting can act. The colour-tube-weighted form of the p-n factor is the same mean, tilted:

  z - h\Bigl(\tfrac{1}{2} - \tfrac{\delta}{4}\Bigr)
  \;=\; w_{p}\, f_{pp} + w_{n}\, f_{nn},
  \qquad
  w_{p} = \tfrac{1}{2} + \tfrac{\delta}{4},
  \quad
  w_{n} = \tfrac{1}{2} - \tfrac{\delta}{4},
  \quad
  w_{p} + w_{n} = 1,

with \delta the substrate flavour split of prop:flavor-split-substrate. A like-flavour bond has no mean to tilt — averaging f_{pp} with itself returns f_{pp} for any weights summing to one — which is why the weighting is defined at the p-n interface and nowhere else.

The tilt is not bar-invariant. \delta is bar-mixed, \overline{\delta} = -q^{2}\delta, and

  \overline{f^{\,\mathrm{weighted}}_{pn}} - f^{\,\mathrm{weighted}}_{pn}
  \;=\; \frac{(q-1)^{5}(q+1)^{3}(q^{2}+1)}{12\,q^{5}},

nonzero for q \neq 1 (about 1.67 \times 10^{-5} at the substrate anchor). The unweighted factor above is the only one of the two that is bar-even, and the derivation in this proof — trace-linearity from the single Markov axiom — yields that one. The weighted form requires \delta as an additional input and is therefore not obtained here.

The obstruction is one factor of q^{2}, and it is repairable

Write a general weighted p-n factor with offset \varepsilon, f_{pn}(\varepsilon) = (\tfrac12 + \varepsilon) f_{pp} + (\tfrac12 - \varepsilon) f_{nn}. Since f_{nn} = \overline{f_{pp}}, the involution swaps the two terms, so

  \overline{f_{pn}} - f_{pn}
  \;=\; -\bigl(\overline{\varepsilon} + \varepsilon\bigr)\,\frac{q^{2}-1}{q},

which vanishes iff \overline{\varepsilon} = -\varepsilon — the offset must be bar-odd. (Not bar-even: symmetrising the weight is the wrong repair.)

The colour weighting uses \varepsilon = \delta/4, and \overline{\delta} = -q^{2}\delta, so it misses bar-oddness by exactly a factor of q^{2} and nothing else. That factor localises: in the factored form \delta \sim \hbar_q^{2}\, h_q\, [2]_q of prop:flavor-split-substrate, the Hecke crossing h_q is already bar-odd and the doublet integer [2]_q is bar-even, so the entire obstruction is the \hbar_q^{2} prefactor — the two quanta of substrate Planck action.

Consequently a bar-invariant colour weighting exists: \varepsilon = q\,\delta\,E/4 is bar-odd for any bar-even E, since \overline{q\delta} = -q\delta. Two natural members are E = 1 and E = [2]_q/2 (the latter being the bar-odd projection of \delta), differing from the current offset by 11–12 % and hence by order 8 \times 10^{-6} in f_{pn}.

Bar-invariance is necessary but not sufficient. It fixes the parity and leaves a whole bar-even function E free, so it does not by itself determine the weighting; selecting E requires re-deriving the colour weighting from the colour-tube geometry, and no particular E is asserted here. All of the above is checked exactly in pn_interface_bar_structure_probe.py (17 assertions), and the four identities that are field-theoretic rather than substrate-specific — \overline{z} = z - h, the bar-symmetriser form, the bar defect -(\overline{\varepsilon} + \varepsilon)h, and the bar-even-iff-offset-bar-odd equivalence — are formalised over an arbitrary characteristic-zero field in QOU/MassTheory/PnInterfaceBarStructure.lean, sorry-free (#print axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only).

Per-atom interface census (from atom_braid_word_3A):

  • D: p \cdot \sigma_3 \cdot n — 1 positive (p-n).
  • T: p \cdot \sigma_3 \cdot n \cdot \sigma_6^{-1} \cdot n — 1 positive (p-n) + 1 negative (n-n).
  • {}^{3}He: p \cdot \sigma_3 \cdot p \cdot \sigma_6 \cdot n — 2 positive (p-p, p-n).
  • {}^{4}He: p \cdot \sigma_3 \cdot p \cdot \sigma_6 \cdot n \cdot \sigma_9^{-1} \cdot n — 2 positive (p-p, p-n) + 1 negative (n-n).

Structural reading

The interface knot \bowtie_K is categorically the Markov-axiom boundary contribution to the canonical atomic braid:

  • Positive interface \sigma_g (p-p or p-n boundary) \to factor z exactly (single application of the Markov axiom).
  • Negative interface \sigma_g^{-1} (n-n boundary, antisymmetric quark pair) \to factor z - h exactly (Markov axiom + Hecke skein \sigma^{-1} = \sigma - h \cdot \mathbf{1}).

The crossing-sign / nucleon-flavor pairing is encoded in \bowtie_K via p_+(K) and p_-(K) counts — these are determined structurally by the canonical-braid construction, not phenomenologically fit.

This locks 's interface-knot factorisation as derivation-grade: each interface in the canonical atomic braid contributes a Markov-trace factor that is either z or z - h, determined by the crossing sign. No empirical-fit parameter remains at the \mathrm{tr}_M level.

Constit-side companion identity (conjectural)

The factorisation (\star) isolates the interface contribution to the \mathrm{tr}_M ratio. The complementary constit factor — \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_K^{\mathrm{vac}}) at varying Z — admits its own clean categorical form at the substrate point:

  \frac{\mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\beta_{(Z+1, N)}^{\mathrm{constit}}\bigr)}
       {\mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\beta_{(Z, N)}^{\mathrm{constit}}\bigr)}
  \;=\; (2q - 1) \,+\, O(h^4)
  \quad\text{at }q_0.

This is the content of conj:constit-factor-2q-minus-1 (0.033\% rel. err.). Combining (\star) with the constit-side conjecture yields the full per-Z \mathrm{tr}_M step

  \frac{\mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_K^{Z+1, N})}{\mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_K^{Z, N})}
  \;=\; z \cdot (2q - 1) \,+\, O(h^4)
  \;=\; \frac{2q - 1}{q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}} \,+\, O(h^4).
